newsitem.title: USA: Gore says Buddhist fundraiser a 'mistake'.
newsitem.headline: Gore says Buddhist fundraiser a 'mistake'.

text.p: Vice President Al Gore admitted on Friday he goofed when he attended a controversial Democratic Party fundraiser at a Buddhist temple last April.
"Well, it was a mistake," Gore said in a taped interview shown on Friday on NBC's "Today" show.
In interviews after articles about the fund-raising event appeared in newspapers during the 1996 presidential campaign, Gore said he did not know there was fund-raising going on at the temple.

"I did not know that it was a fund-raiser. But I knew it was a political event," he added on Friday. "And I knew that there were finance people who were going to be present. And so that alone should have told me this is inappropriate -- and this is a mistake -- don't do this. And I take responsibility for that. It was a mistake."

The fund-raiser at the tax-exempt Los Angeles area temple became a major issue in the presidential campaign and was part of a series of disputed money-raising efforts by the Democrats that have come under fire and will be the focus of congressional investigations. The Justice Department is also investigating Democratic fund-raising that includes money raised improperly from foreign nationals.

Some $140,000 was raised at the Buddhist temple event organised in part by former Democratic Party official John Huang, a one-time employee of the Lippo Group financial empire of Indonesia. Huang is at the centre of investigations of fund-raising activities.
The party has returned some $1.5 million in improper or questionable funds following news reports about foreign-linked contributions.
